content.title: Phase-State Opponent | Contact Dispersal and Reassembly Reversal
content.summary: Keep one adult physical protagonist and one phase-changing opponent on a stable attack axis. Every decisive contact begins a directional material change at the hit point, retained matter visibly rebuilds the same opponent, local deformation escalates to full-body dispersal, and an apparent terminal burst reverses through reassembly in an established zone.

quick_start.input_format: clearly adult physical protagonist and original phase-changing opponent on one stable attack axis + every decisive contact starts strands, particles or fluid change at the hit point + displaced matter remains visible and rebuilds the same opponent + local deformation escalates to full-body dispersal + apparent terminal burst reverses through reassembly in an established zone
quick_start.recommended_input: An adult salvage technician fights an original scrap sentinel in one dry-dock lane. Wrench impacts scatter only contacted metal into retained flakes, the same flakes reconnect, a final full-body burst appears decisive, and retained filings rebuild the sentinel behind the technician.
required_anchors: Establish both clearly adult subjects, one ground plane and one attack axis before the first close contact.
Bind every decisive hit to a directional phase change beginning at the visible contact point.
Escalate from local deformation to at least one full-body dispersal while retaining ground and light anchors.
After an apparent terminal burst, reassemble the opponent inside a previously established zone.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Keep one adult physical protagonist and one phase-changing opponent on a stable attack axis. Every decisive contact begins a directional material change at the hit point, retained matter visibly rebuilds the same opponent, local deformation escalates to full-body dispersal, and an apparent terminal burst reverses through reassembly in an established zone.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish one original clearly adult physical protagonist and one original phase-changing opponent on a stable attack axis before close combat begins. Bind every decisive contact to a directional material response: the opponent must visibly transition from coherent silhouette into strands, particles or fluid-like mass at the contact point, keep that displaced material inside the shared geography, then rebuild from it rather than respawning. Escalate from local deformation to full-body dispersal while preserving ground, light direction and subject positions as continuity anchors. End after the apparent terminal burst by reassembling the opponent in a previously established zone. The reusable mechanism is contact-driven phase change, retained material continuity, escalating dispersal scale and post-victory reassembly—not the source fighters, masks, costumes, weapons, desert, dust palette, choreography, framing, watermark, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Establish both clearly adult subjects, one ground plane and one attack axis before the first close contact.
invariants.purpose: Creates spatial proof for later deformation and recovery.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without a stable baseline, particle motion cannot be tied to either combatant.

invariants.rule: Bind every decisive hit to a directional phase change beginning at the visible contact point.
invariants.purpose: Makes the supernatural response a physical consequence of action.
invariants.ablation_failure: A detached effect cloud reads as decoration rather than damage or defense.

invariants.rule: Keep displaced strands or particles visible until they reconnect into the same opponent.
invariants.purpose: Preserves material conservation and identity continuity.
invariants.ablation_failure: A clean disappearance followed by a fresh body reads as a reset.

invariants.rule: Escalate from local deformation to at least one full-body dispersal while retaining ground and light anchors.
invariants.purpose: Raises threat scale without losing combat geography.
invariants.ablation_failure: Random spectacle or location changes break the progression.

invariants.rule: After an apparent terminal burst, reassemble the opponent inside a previously established zone.
invariants.purpose: Turns phase control into the final narrative proof.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending before reassembly reduces the mechanism to ordinary defeat.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source masked muscular fighter, dark reaper-like opponent, faces, bodies, costumes and weapon shapes
the source desert plain, sunset backlight, brown dust density, horizon and exact terrain
the source black tendrils, scythe-like limb, sand-body effect and exact transformation appearance
the source kicks, punches, throws, aerial attacks, catches, close choreography, camera path and 26-second timing
the source creator identity, TECHHALLA watermark, Seedance 2.5 claim, prompt wording and branding
